newsitem.title: USA: Nasdaq finishes higher, inches toward record.
newsitem.headline: Nasdaq finishes higher, inches toward record.

text.p: Nasdaq stocks extended their gains to three straight sessions Thursday as the brightening outlook for high technology investments carried the market higher.
The Nasdaq Composite Index added 8.6 points, or 0.7 percent, to end unoffically at 1254.1, four points short of the measure's all-time closing high.
Gainers outpaced decliners by 11 to 10, while the session yielded 188 new highs and 139 new lows. Unofficial volume was about 670 million shares.

Traders said Intel Corp's forecast of improved fourth quarter revenues and gross margin versus the prior period was among the latest and most significant indicators of robust future performance for U.S. tech companies.

Arnie Owen, Kaufman Brothers director of equities, said, "Technology was strong right up to the last five minutes when a little profit taking came in. Proposition 211 was defeated, and last night Intel -- because the shackles were taken off -- said everything looks good."
Intel added 3-1/4 to 122-1/8 and was the market's most active issue, followed by Cisco Systems, up 3-1/4 to 64-1/2. -- B. Intindola, Wall Street Desk, 212-859-1734.
